title_en: Yamaha Corporation v. Gangtian Group Company, Gangtian Co., Ltd. — trademark infringement dispute
keywords_en: civil; dispute over infringement of exclusive right to use a trademark; first instance; High People's Court; Tianjin; legal person; foreign-invested enterprise; Trademark Law; determination of trademark infringement; joint tort liability; false advertising; motorcycle manufacturing; trademark use; product catalogue listing; tort liability; dispute over infringement of exclusive right to use a trademark by a limited company
full_text_en:
Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. v. Gangtian Group Company,
Gangtian Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of trademark exclusive right

Plaintiff: Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. Domicile: Iwata City, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan.
Legal Representative: Hasegawa Itaru, President of the Company.

Defendant: Tianjin Gangtian Group Company. Domicile: Shuanggang Town, Jinnan District, Tianjin.
Legal Representative: Gong Zhaoshan, Chairman of the Company.

Defendant: Tianjin Gangtian Engine Co., Ltd. Domicile: Shuanggang Town, Jinnan District, Tianjin.
Legal Representative: He Wanli, Chairman of the Company.

The plaintiff, Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yamaha), filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin High People's Court against the defendants, Tianjin Gangtian Group Company (hereinafter referred to as Gangtian Group) and Tianjin Gangtian Engine Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gangtian Co., Ltd.), concerning a dispute over infringement of trademark exclusive right.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff registered the trademarks "YAMAHA" and "VISION" in China and enjoys the exclusive right to use these trademarks in accordance with the law. The engines of the Gangtian brand GT125T, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A two-wheel motorcycles produced and sold by the two defendants all bear the "YAMAHA" trademark logo. The defendants' actions constitute an infringement of the plaintiff's registered trademark by unauthorized use, and they should bear joint civil liability for the infringement.

The content registered by the defendant Gangtian Group in the "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products" for the Gangtian GT125T, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A models, stating that they use "Linhai YAMAHA" brand LY152QMI and LYIE40QMB engines, does not match the facts. Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. does not produce "Linhai YAMAHA" brand LY152QMI and LYIE40QMB engines. This registered content constitutes false advertising and should be deleted in accordance with the law.

The plaintiff's claims are:
1. The two defendants shall immediately cease infringing upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademarks.
2. The two defendants shall jointly and severally compensate the plaintiff for the economic losses of RMB 10,000,000 caused by their infringement of the plaintiff's trademark exclusive right.
3. The two defendants shall publish a public apology in newspapers distributed nationwide to eliminate the adverse effects.
4. The defendant Gangtian Group shall delete the content from the "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products" regarding "GT125T, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A motorcycles using Linhai YAMAHA brand LY152QMI and LYIE40QMB engines."
5. The two defendants shall bear all litigation costs of this case.

The plaintiff submitted the following evidence to prove the facts it alleged:

1. Trademark registration certificates for "YAMAHA" and "VISION" issued by the Trademark Office of the People's Republic of China to the plaintiff, proving the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the "YAMAHA" and "VISION" trademarks. The "List of Key Trademarks Under National Protection" published by the competent authority of China in June 2000 proves that "YAMAHA" falls within the scope of national key trademark protection.

2. Promotional materials of Southern Zhuzhou-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. and articles and advertisements in magazines "Motorcycle" and "Motorcycle Information" introducing motorcycles using the "VISION" trademark, proving that the enterprise in which Yamaha has a joint venture in China for producing 125-model motorcycles is Zhuzhou Southern-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., and its ZY125 model motorcycle uses the "VISION" trademark. This model was exhibited at the Guangdong Motorcycle Show in November 2000. The plaintiff had not authorized any other Chinese enterprise to use this trademark.

3. In April 2000, the plaintiff's agent purchased three Gangtian brand GT125T, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A two-wheel motorcycles from the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., and requested the Beijing Chang'an Notary Office to notarize and seal the said motorcycles. In the toolkit of the GT50T-A model motorcycle, there were a Gangtian motorcycle instruction manual and a Gangtian brand motorcycle certificate of quality. The instruction manual stated the manufacturer was the defendant Gangtian Group and the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. The certificate of quality bore the seal "Special Seal for Finished Product Quality Inspection of Tianjin Gangtian Group Company". Transparent adhesive stickers reading "engine licensed YAMAHA" were affixed to the front and rear body of the motorcycle, with the "engine licensed" in smaller font and "YAMAHA" in larger font. The end cover of the engine was cast with the "licensed YAMAHA" logo. The above evidence proves that the two defendants jointly produced and sold infringing products, infringing the plaintiff's trademark exclusive right.

4. The Administrative Penalty Decision No. 008 (2000) of the Tianjin Administration for Industry and Commerce, Jinnan Sub-bureau, and on-site photos of the workshop of the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., prove that the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. used the "VISION" logo on the fuel tanks of 37 GT125-6 type motorcycles it produced; and that the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. produced GT50T-A type motorcycles, with transparent adhesive stickers reading "engine licensed YAMAHA" affixed to the front and rear body.

5. The "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products", two records of interviews conducted by the Qidong Administration for Industry and Commerce of Jiangsu Province with employees of Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., a reply from Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. to the Qidong AIC, a reply from the Beijing Office of Yamaha Motor Corporation of Japan to the Qidong AIC, and a certificate issued by Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. The above documentary evidence proves that in the said catalogue, the defendant Gangtian Group registered the following content for GT125T, GT125T-A, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A motorcycles: the manufacturer is Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., the trademark of the engine is "Linhai YAMAHA", and the engine models are LY152QMI (153FM) and LYIE40QMB (IE40FM). However, Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., as a joint venture of the plaintiff, does not produce or sell LY152QMI and LYIE40QMB engines. The above evidence proves that the defendant Gangtian Group used the said catalogue to improperly use the plaintiff's trademark for false advertising.

6. A statistical table showing the decrease in sales of the plaintiff's joint venture in China, Zhuzhou Southern-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., and a statement of expenses incurred by the plaintiff in investigating and stopping the infringement by the two defendants, proving the losses caused to the plaintiff by the infringement and the basis for the claim.

Defendant Gangtian Group's Defense: The infringing products mentioned in the plaintiff's complaint were not actually manufactured by the defendant Gangtian Group. The company only learned of the infringing acts of the second defendant, Gangtian Co., Ltd., after the administrative authority made an administrative penalty decision against Gangtian Co., Ltd. The company applied for the catalogue entry strictly in accordance with the procedures and materials required by national regulations, based on the "Industrial and Mineral Products Purchase and Sale Contract" signed at the time of purchasing the engines. Therefore, the company has not infringed the plaintiff's trademark exclusive right and should not bear any liability for compensation.

Defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd.'s Defense: The company has never produced GT125T-B type motorcycles, nor does it produce GT125T motorcycles. The GT125-6 type motorcycles were produced by the company without knowing that "VISION" was the plaintiff's trademark. Only 50 units were produced, and before any sale, the company was penalized by the administrative authority. The products did not enter the market and did not cause losses to the plaintiff. The engines used in the GT50T-A type motorcycles produced by the company were purchased from a manufacturer authorized by the plaintiff. Therefore, the use of "engine licensed YAMAHA" on the motorcycle body and engine was lawful.

The defendants Gangtian Group and Gangtian Co., Ltd. submitted the following evidence to prove the facts they alleged:

1. The Administrative Penalty Decision No. 008 (2000) of Tianjin Administration for Industry and Commerce, Jinnan Sub-bureau. This decision identified and penalized the infringer as the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., to prove that the defendant Gangtian Group did not infringe.

2. An agreement signed on July 27, 1999, between Gangtian Co., Ltd. and Southern Motorcycle Co., Ltd. for the purchase of 1,111 NF1E40QMB engines for GT50T-A type motorcycles, and four VAT invoices for the performance of this agreement, to prove that the use of "engine licensed YAMAHA" on the front and rear body of the GT50T-A type motorcycle it produced was lawful.

3. The "Industrial and Mineral Products Purchase and Sale Contract" signed between the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. and Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. for the purchase of 135FM and IE40FM engines, and a fax copy of one VAT invoice for the performance of this contract, to prove that the defendant Gangtian Group strictly applied for the catalogue entry in accordance with the procedures and materials required by national regulations, and that the registration of the use of LY125-QMI and LYIE40QMB engines in the catalogue had a legal basis.

4. A certificate and delivery note issued by Tianjin Junlida Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., to prove that the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. purchased finished fuel tanks from Tianjin Junlida Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., and these finished fuel tanks bore the "VISION" logo, a fact confirmed by the administrative penalty decision.

5. Uniform receipts for confiscated property in Tianjin, to prove that the 37 GT125-6 type motorcycles produced by the two defendants were sealed before sale and did not generate any profit.

Facts Found by the Tianjin High People's Court:

The plaintiff registered the trademarks "YAMAHA" and "VISION" with the Trademark Office of the People's Republic of China on March 14, 1999, and June 21, 1999, respectively. The designated goods are in Class 12, including motorcycles, fuel tanks for motorcycles, engines for land vehicles, and motorcycle parts. In June 2000, the competent authority of China published the "List of Key Trademarks Under National Protection," which included the "YAMAHA" trademark among motorcycle products.

On July 27, 1999, the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. signed an agreement with Southern Motorcycle Co., Ltd. to purchase 1,111 NFIE40QMB engines for GT50T-A type motorcycles. The agreement was fully performed on September 21, 1999. The end covers of these engines left the factory cast with the words "licensed YAMAHA". The defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., on the outer packaging and body of the GT50T-A type motorcycles it produced, indicated "Gangtian Brand" GT50T-A motorcycle in the corresponding parts as required by national standards. At the same time, the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. affixed transparent adhesive stickers reading "engine licensed YAMAHA" to the front and rear body of the GT50T-A type motorcycles it produced. The sticker text was in two lines, with "engine licensed" in a smaller font on the top line and "YAMAHA" in a relatively larger font on the bottom line. The font size of "YAMAHA" was approximately three times larger than that of "engine licensed".

On April 10, 2000, the plaintiff requested the Beijing Chang'an Notary Office to notarize and seal three Gangtian motorcycles sold by the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. Upon inspection of the sealed packages, the three motor models were GT125T, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A two-wheel motorcycles. Among them, the front and rear body of the GT50T-A motorcycle bore the words "engine licensed YAMAHA". The instruction manual stated that the manufacturer was the defendant Gangtian Group and the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., and it was accompanied by a "Tianjin Gangtian Motorcycle Certificate of Quality", which bore the seal "Special Seal for Finished Product Quality Inspection of Tianjin Gangtian Group Company". On June 27, 2000, the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. purchased 50 fuel tanks for GT125-6 type motorcycles from Tianjin Junlida Industry and Trade Co., Ltd., accompanied by 50 "VISION" logos. The defendant Gangtian Engine Company used the "VISION" logo on the fuel tanks of 37 GT125-6 type motorcycles it produced. Consequently, the defendant Gangtian Engine Company was subjected to an administrative penalty by the Tianjin Administration for Industry and Commerce, Jinnan Sub-bureau, on September 1, 2000.

One of the plaintiff Yamaha's joint ventures in China for producing 125-type motorcycles is Zhuzhou Southern-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. The ZY125 model motorcycle it produces uses the cursive "VISION" trademark on its fuel tank. This model was exhibited at the Guangdong Motorcycle Show in 2000 and was featured in introductory articles and product advertisements in magazines such as "Motorcycle" and "Motorcycle Information".

Additionally, in March 1999, the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. signed an "Industrial and Mineral Products Purchase and Sale Contract" with Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. to purchase 2,000 153FM engines for the 125 series and 500 IE40FM engines for the 50 series. This contract was not actually performed. Despite this, Gangtian Group, based on this contract, registered the following content in the "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products" for the GT125T, GT125T-A, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A models: the manufacturer was the defendant Gangtian Group, the engine manufacturer was Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., the engine trademark was "Linhai YAMAHA", and the engine models were LY152QMI (153FM) and LYIE40QMB (IE40FM). Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., as a joint venture of Yamaha in China, only produces engines for the 90 and 100 series motorcycles and is permitted by the plaintiff to use the "LINHAI-YAMAHA" logo; it does not produce "Linhai YAMAHA" brand LY152QMI and LYIE40QMB engines.

The evidence used to prove the above facts was presented, examined, and cross-examined by the parties in court, and was admitted by the Tianjin High People's Court.

The main issues disputed by the parties during the trial were:

1. Whether the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd.'s use of the "VISION" logo on the fuel tanks of GT125-6 type motorcycles and its use of stickers reading "engine licensed YAMAHA" on the front and rear body of GT50T-A type motorcycles constituted infringement.
2. Whether the defendants Gangtian Group and Gangtian Co., Ltd. constituted joint infringement.
3. Whether Gangtian Group engaged in false advertising through the "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products".
4. The factual and legal basis for the plaintiff's claim for compensation of RMB 10,000,000 from the two defendants in this case.

Opinion of the Tianjin High People's Court:

The conduct in dispute in this case occurred before the implementation of the revised Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, and therefore, the relevant provisions of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China in force at the time shall apply. Article 38 of that Law stipulates: "Any of the following acts shall be an infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark..." Paragraph (1) states: "using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same goods or similar goods without the authorization of the registrant." Paragraph (2) states: "selling goods that he knows bear a counterfeit registered trademark."

The "YAMAHA" and "VISION" trademarks registered by the plaintiff in the People's Republic of China shall be protected by law. The defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., without the plaintiff's authorization, affixed the words "engine licensed YAMAHA" to the front and rear body areas of the GT50T-A type motorcycles it produced, deliberately enlarging the display of the "YAMAHA" font. This was clearly an attempt to take advantage of Chinese consumers' unfamiliarity with English or their negligence, implying some connection between its own products and "YAMAHA". Therefore, the behavior of the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. constitutes using the plaintiff's registered trademark on identical goods without authorization, and thus infringes upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark.

Zhuzhou Southern-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd.'s use of the "VISION" trademark in a prominent position on the fuel tank of its ZY125 model motorcycle was authorized by the plaintiff. This model participated in the Guangdong Motorcycle Show and was featured in numerous articles and advertisements. The defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd., without the authorization of Yamaha, used the "VISION" trademark in the same manner on the fuel tank of its self-manufactured GT125-6 model motorcycle, thereby infringing upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark. Gangtian Co., Ltd.'s defense regarding the source of the fuel tanks does not affect the finding of infringement by the company.

The content registered by the defendant Gangtian Group in the "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products" for the Gangtian GT125T, GT125T-A, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A models included the engine manufacturer as Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., the engine trademark as "Linhai YAMAHA", and the engine models as LY152QMI and LYIE40QMB. Although the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. signed an agreement with Jiangsu Linhai-Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. to purchase the above engines, the evidence provided by Gangtian Group and Gangtian Co., Ltd. regarding the performance of the contract was insufficient. Therefore, their argument that there was a legal basis for the engines registered in the catalogue products cannot be established. Considering all the facts of the case, it should be determined that the defendant Gangtian Group also used the contract and product catalogue to employ the "YAMAHA" trademark text to promote its own products. This use by the defendant Gangtian Group also constitutes trademark infringement.

The instruction manual and product certificate of quality for the infringing products involved in this case, as well as the "National Catalogue of Automobiles, Modified Civil Vehicles, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Products," all indicate that the defendant Gangtian Group is the manufacturer of the motorcycles. Furthermore, the defendant Gangtian Group independently applied for the catalogue entry from the national administrative authority in the name of the manufacturer. This proves that the defendant Gangtian Group and the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. were both manufacturers of the infringing products, constituting joint infringement, and they shall bear tort liability. The defendants' defense that the products did not generate profit and therefore refused to pay compensation cannot be established.

The primary evidence submitted by the plaintiff in support of its claim for damages consisted of statistical data showing a decrease in sales volume of Zhuzhou Southern Yamaha Motorcycle Co., Ltd. and the relevant expenses incurred by the plaintiff in investigating and stopping the infringement by the two defendants, including attorneys' fees and advertising costs. However, the plaintiff did not provide original vouchers, and the evidence lacks probative force; therefore, it is not admitted. It should be considered that the defendants' infringing conduct might have been a factor contributing to the decrease in sales of the plaintiff's joint venture products, indirectly harming the plaintiff's interests as a shareholder of the joint venture. However, an increase or decrease in sales volume is influenced by multiple market factors, and the defendants' infringing conduct was not the sole factor. Therefore, the impact of the defendants' infringing conduct on the sales volume of the plaintiff's joint venture is difficult to use as direct evidence of damages. The attorneys' fees paid by the plaintiff in connection with this case, based on the materials provided by the plaintiff, are difficult to determine as a reasonable amount; the advertising expenses already incurred also include content unrelated to this case. Consequently, the amount of damages claimed by the plaintiff lacks sufficient evidence. Nevertheless, the plaintiff's reasonable claims regarding the scope of damages may be considered as factors in determining the amount of damages to be paid by the defendants in this case. Given that the amount of loss caused by the defendants' infringing conduct in this case is difficult to determine, the amount of damages is determined in accordance with the principles of tort compensation and fairness and good faith under the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, taking into account relevant reasonable factors and circumstances pertaining to the compensation.

In conclusion, the Tianjin High People's Court, pursuant to Article 38, items (1) and (2), and Article 39 of the *Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China*, rendered the following judgment on August 6, 2002:

1. The defendant Gangtian Group Company and the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease the sale of motorcycles bearing the "VIS ION" trademark model; and shall immediately cease the sale of motorcycles bearing the words "engine licensed by YAMAHA" on the front and rear body panels.

2. The defendant Gangtian Group Company and the defendant Gangtian Co., Ltd. shall, within fifteen days from the date this judgment takes effect, jointly and severally pay Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. RMB 400,000.

3. The defendant Gangtian Group Company is ordered, within sixty days from the date this judgment takes effect, to apply to the national administrative department in charge of the *Directory of National Automotive, Modified Vehicle, and Motorcycle Manufacturers and Product Catalogues* to amend the registration information for motorcycle models GT125T, GT125T-A, GT125T-B, and GT50T-A, changing the "engine manufacturer" to Jiangsu Linhai Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd., the "engine trademark" to "Linhai YAMAHA", and the "engine model" to LY152QMI (153FM) and LYIE40QMB (IE40FM).

4. The defendant Gangtian Group Company shall, within sixty days from the date this judgment takes effect, publish an apology to the plaintiff Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. in *Motorcycle* magazine, with the content of the apology subject to approval by the Tianjin High People's Court. In case of default, the Tianjin High People's Court shall publicly announce this judgment, and the publication costs shall be borne by the defendant Gangtian Group Company.

5. The remaining claims of the plaintiff Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 60,010 shall be borne by the plaintiff Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 12,002, and by the defendants Gangtian Group Company and Gangtian Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 24,004 each.

After the judgment was announced, none of the parties filed an appeal, and the judgment of first instance has taken legal effect.
